title: Nice to Meet You!
grammar_topic: Verb to be: afirmativo, negativo y preguntas
can_do: Puede saludar, presentarse, decir quién es y de dónde es

grammar_explanation.core_rule: El verbo 'to be' (ser/estar) cambia según la persona: am, is, are. En español muchas veces no se necesita un verbo para presentarse ('Yo, Camila'), pero en inglés el verbo 'to be' SIEMPRE tiene que aparecer.

structure_notes.label: I
structure_notes.explanation: am / am not / Am I...?
structure_notes.example: I am Camila. I'm not a teacher. Am I late?

structure_notes.label: You
structure_notes.explanation: are / aren't / Are you...?
structure_notes.example: You are a student. You aren't from here. Are you ready?

structure_notes.label: He / She / It
structure_notes.explanation: is / isn't / Is he...?
structure_notes.example: She is a teacher. He isn't from Madrid. Is it far?

structure_notes.label: We / You / They
structure_notes.explanation: are / aren't / Are we...?
structure_notes.example: We are friends. They aren't students. Are we late?

examples: I am Camila. (Soy Camila.)
She is a teacher. (Ella es profesora.)
They are not from Tokyo. (Ellos no son de Tokyo.)
Are you a student? (¿Eres estudiante?)
grammar_explanation.common_mistake: El error más común de hispanohablantes es OMITIR el verbo 'to be' ('Yo profesora' en vez de 'I am a teacher'). En inglés el verbo siempre va.

grammar_practice.q: My teacher _____ from the United States.
'He are my friend' is grammatically correct.
Empareja el pronombre con su forma de 'to be'

vocabulary.example: Hello! How are you?
Good morning, everyone.
Hi Daniel, how are you?
Nice to meet you, Daniel.
My name is Camila.
Hi, what's your name?
I'm from Madrid.
Where are you from, Marta?
She is my English teacher.
I am a new student.
He is my friend from university.
Goodbye, see you tomorrow!

vocab_practice.q: What does 'Nice to meet you' mean?
Empareja la frase con su significado
Choose the correct response to 'Nice to meet you.'
___ are you from? — I'm from Toronto.
Which greeting is correct for the morning?
Empareja el saludo con la respuesta correcta

reading.title: Hi, I'm Camila
reading.text: Hi! My name is Camila and I am from Madrid. I am a student at a language school. My teacher's name is Mr. Rojas, and he is from the United States. My best friend at school is Daniel. He is not from Madrid; he is from Sydney. We are in the same class every morning. In my class, we are all beginners in English, but we are not shy! Every day we say 'Good morning' and practice new words together. I am very happy at this school.

questions.q: Where is Camila from?
What is Camila?
Is Daniel from Madrid?
How does Camila feel at the school?
Empareja la persona con su origen

reading.title: My New Classmate
reading.text: Today is my first day at Tweetalig. My name is Julian, and I am from Toronto. There is a new student next to me. Her name is Valentina. She is from Madrid, but she is not new to English — she is at a high level already! Our teacher is Miss Paola. She is very patient and friendly. Valentina and I are both nervous, but we are excited too. 'Nice to meet you,' Valentina says. 'Nice to meet you too,' I say. I think we are going to be good friends this year.

questions.q: Where is Julian from?
Is Valentina new to English?
What is the teacher's name?
How do Julian and Valentina feel?
___ this Julian's first day? (completa con Is/Are)

listening.title: Meeting at Orientation
listening.transcript:
A: Hi! My name is Sofia. What's your name?
B: Hi, Sofia! I'm Andres. Nice to meet you.
A: Nice to meet you too! Where are you from?
B: I'm from Toronto. And you?
A: I'm from Madrid. Are you a new student here?
B: Yes, I am! This is my first day.
A: Me too! Good luck, Andres.
B: Thanks, Sofia. See you in class!

questions.q: What is the woman's name?
Where is Andres from?
Is this Andres's first day?
What does Sofia say at the end?
Is Sofia a new student too?
Empareja el hablante con su ciudad
___ you a new student? (completa)

listening.title: My New Neighbor
listening.transcript: Let me tell you about my new neighbor. Her name is Laura, and she is from Madrid. Yesterday, she came to say hello to my family. This is my wife, Ana, and this is our friend, Carlos — they are not from Madrid, they are from Toronto, like me. Laura is very nice, and she is happy to be here. She says our street is quiet and friendly. I think Laura is going to be a great neighbor.

questions.q: What is the new neighbor's name?
Where is Laura from?
Is Carlos the speaker's wife?
Who is Ana?
How does Laura feel about being there?
The street ___ quiet and friendly. (completa con is/are)

prompt.en: Introduce yourself. Write 3 to 5 sentences using the verb 'to be'. Say: your name, where you're from, what you are (student/teacher/etc.) and something else about you.
prompt.es: Preséntate. Escribe de 3 a 5 oraciones usando el verbo 'to be'. Di: tu nombre, de dónde eres, qué eres (estudiante/profesor/etc.) y algo más sobre ti.

rubric.descripcion: Incluye nombre, origen y ocupación.
Usa am/is/are correctamente según la persona.
Usa al menos 2 palabras de la lista.
Las oraciones tienen sentido y se conectan.

'Nice to meet you' is a greeting for meeting someone for the first time.

Empareja el pronombre con su forma de 'to be'

title: Transportation
can_do: Puede hablar de personas y objetos y desenvolverse en transporte

grammar_explanation.core_rule: Los pronombres cambian de forma según su función en la oración: sujeto (quién hace la acción), objeto (quién recibe la acción), y posesivo (de quién es algo).

structure_notes.label: Pronombres de sujeto
structure_notes.explanation: I, you, he, she, it, we, they — van antes del verbo.
structure_notes.example: She takes the bus every morning.

structure_notes.label: Pronombres de objeto
structure_notes.explanation: me, you, him, her, it, us, them — van después del verbo o de una preposición.
structure_notes.example: The driver helps her with the bags.

structure_notes.label: Adjetivos posesivos
structure_notes.explanation: my, your, his, her, its, our, their — van antes de un sustantivo.
structure_notes.example: This is my bicycle.

examples: He drives to work every day.
Can you help me, please?
This is her bicycle.
We take our bags with us.
grammar_explanation.common_mistake: Confundir 'his' y 'her' — muchos hispanohablantes usan 'his' para todo. 'His' es de él, 'her' es de ella, sin importar el género del objeto.

grammar_practice.q: The taxi driver talks to ___. (a nosotros)
Can you drive _____ to the station?
'Her' can be used before a noun, like 'her car'.
Empareja el pronombre de sujeto con su forma de objeto

My father drives a car.

reading.title: Going to School by Bus
reading.text: Every morning, Julian takes the bus to school. He waits for it at the corner near his house. The bus driver is very kind, and he always says hello to him. Today, there are many passengers on the bus, and there is a lot of traffic. Julian looks out the window and sees his friend Marta. She is riding her bicycle. He waves at her. The bus arrives at school at 7:30. Julian is never late because his bus is always on time. He likes taking the bus with his classmates every day.

questions.q: How does Julian go to school?
Is the bus driver kind?
What does Julian see out the window?
What time does the bus arrive at school?
Is Julian usually late?

reading.title: My Sister's Bicycle
reading.text: My sister Valentina has a new bicycle. It is blue and very fast. She rides it to work every day because there is always a lot of traffic in our city. I usually take the bus, but sometimes I take a taxi if I am late. Valentina says her bicycle is better than a car because she never waits in traffic. Our father drives his car to work, and he says he wants a bicycle too. Maybe next year we will all ride bicycles together on the weekend.

questions.q: What color is Valentina's bicycle?
Why does Valentina prefer her bicycle?
How does the writer usually travel?
Does their father want a bicycle too?
___ drives his car to work. (completa con el pronombre correcto)

listening.title: Taking a Taxi
listening.transcript:
A: Good morning! Where do you want to go?
B: Hello! I need to go to the airport, please.
A: OK, no problem. Is this your first time in Madrid?
B: Yes, it is! I'm here for work.
A: Great! There is a little traffic today, so it might take twenty minutes.
B: That's fine. Thank you.
A: You're welcome. Please put on your seatbelt.

questions.q: Where does the passenger want to go?
Is this the passenger's first time in Madrid?
Why might the trip take twenty minutes?
What does the driver ask the passenger to do?
Is the passenger here on vacation?
___ this your first time in Madrid? (completa)
Empareja quién dice qué

listening.title: A Bad Morning
listening.transcript: This morning was not easy for me. I missed my bus, so I had to take a taxi instead. It was expensive, but I couldn't be late for work. There was a lot of traffic on the road, so the taxi driver had to take a different street. I was very nervous, but I arrived on time! Next time, I want to leave my house earlier so I don't miss the bus again.

questions.q: What happened to the speaker this morning?
What did they do instead?
Was the taxi expensive?
Was there a lot of traffic?
Did the speaker arrive on time?
I couldn't be late ___ work. (completa la preposición)

title: Restaurants
grammar_topic: Singular/plural nouns; there is/there are; artículos
can_do: Puede describir lo que hay en un lugar y hablar de comida/restaurantes

grammar_explanation.core_rule: Usamos 'there is' con sustantivos singulares y 'there are' con plurales para decir que algo existe en un lugar. Los artículos 'a/an' se usan para algo no específico, 'the' para algo específico ya mencionado o conocido.

structure_notes.label: there is + singular
structure_notes.explanation: Para un solo objeto o persona.
structure_notes.example: There is a table by the window.

structure_notes.label: there are + plural
structure_notes.explanation: Para varios objetos o personas.
structure_notes.example: There are three chairs here.

structure_notes.label: a / an
structure_notes.explanation: 'a' antes de sonido consonante, 'an' antes de sonido vocal.
structure_notes.example: I would like an orange juice and a sandwich.

structure_notes.label: plural de sustantivos
structure_notes.explanation: Se agrega -s a la mayoría de sustantivos.
structure_notes.example: table → tables, dish → dishes

examples: There is a menu on the table.
There are two waiters today.
I would like an orange juice.
The restaurant is very popular.
grammar_explanation.common_mistake: Usar 'there is' con sustantivos plurales: 'there is two tables' es incorrecto — debe ser 'there are two tables'.

grammar_practice.q: There ___ a menu on the table. (is/are)
There ___ a chef in the kitchen.
There ___ five tables in this restaurant.
Can I have ___ orange juice, please? (a/an)
There ___ two desserts on the menu.
There ___ a bill on the table.
There ___ many dishes to choose from.
There _____ a table for two available.
There _____ four forks on the table.
There _____ a waiter near the door.
We use 'an' before a word that starts with a vowel sound.
Empareja el sustantivo con su plural

The waiter is very friendly.

vocab_practice.q: Who cooks the food in a restaurant?
Can I see the ___, please? (lo que muestra los platos disponibles)
Empareja la palabra con su significado

For ___, I want ice cream. (lo dulce al final)
Empareja el utensilio con su uso

reading.title: Lunch at Mama Rosa's
reading.text: Today, my family is having lunch at Mama Rosa's restaurant. There is a nice table for four near the window. Our waiter brings us the menu. There are many delicious dishes to choose from. My mother orders a soup, and my father orders fish with rice. I want a sandwich and an orange juice. There are also many desserts on the menu. My sister orders a chocolate cake for dessert. The chef at Mama Rosa's is very famous in our city. At the end, the waiter brings us the bill, and we pay together.

What does the father order?
Is the chef famous?
What does the sister order for dessert?
There ___ many delicious dishes. (completa)

reading.title: A New Restaurant in Town
reading.text: There is a new restaurant near my house. There are five tables and a small kitchen. The chef is young, but he is very talented. There is a short menu with only ten dishes, but everything is delicious. Yesterday, I ordered a soup and a sandwich. My friend ordered a salad. There wasn't a long wait for our food. At the end, the bill was not expensive. I think this restaurant is going to be very popular soon. There are already many customers every day.

Is the chef old?
How many dishes are on the menu?
What did the writer order?

listening.title: Ordering Food
listening.transcript:
A: Good afternoon! Are you ready to order?
B: Yes, I am. Can I have the chicken with rice, please?
A: Of course. Would you like a drink with that?
B: Yes, an orange juice, please.
A: Great. And for dessert?
B: There is a chocolate cake on the menu, right? I'll have that.
A: Perfect choice! It will be ready in fifteen minutes.
B: Thank you very much.

listening.title: A Great Dinner
listening.transcript: Last night, I had dinner at a new restaurant with my family. The food was delicious! I ordered fish, and it was excellent. For dessert, we had chocolate cake, and it was amazing too. At the end, we asked for the bill. It wasn't very expensive, so we were happy. The restaurant accepts cash and cards, so I paid with my card. I think we are going back to that restaurant very soon.

Was the food good?
How did the speaker pay?
Does the restaurant accept cash and cards?
What was amazing according to the speaker?
The restaurant ___ cash and cards. (completa con accepts/accept)

title: Crime
can_do: Puede responder preguntas simples, identificar objetos y hablar de situaciones relacionadas con delitos

grammar_explanation.core_rule: Las respuestas cortas con 'to be' repiten el verbo, no toda la oración ('Are you a witness? Yes, I am.'). Los demostrativos this/that/these/those señalan objetos: this/these para algo cerca, that/those para algo lejos; this/that son singulares, these/those son plurales.

structure_notes.label: Respuestas cortas afirmativas
structure_notes.explanation: Yes, + sujeto + am/is/are.
structure_notes.example: Is this your wallet? Yes, it is.

structure_notes.label: Respuestas cortas negativas
structure_notes.explanation: No, + sujeto + am not/isn't/aren't.
structure_notes.example: Are you a witness? No, I'm not.

structure_notes.label: this / that (singular)
structure_notes.explanation: 'this' para algo cerca, 'that' para algo lejos.
structure_notes.example: This is my ID. That is the police station.

structure_notes.label: these / those (plural)
structure_notes.explanation: 'these' para varios cerca, 'those' para varios lejos.
structure_notes.example: These are my keys. Those are the suspects.

examples: Is this your wallet? Yes, it is.
Are you a witness? No, I'm not.
This is a police officer.
Those are stolen bikes.
grammar_explanation.common_mistake: Usar 'this/that' con sustantivos plurales — 'this bikes' es incorrecto, debe ser 'these bikes'.

grammar_practice.q: Is this your wallet? Yes, it ___.
Are you a witness? No, I'm ___.
Is he a police officer? Yes, he ___.
___ is the police station. (algo lejos, singular)
___ are the suspects over there. (algo lejos, plural)
Is this a crime? Yes, it ___.
Are those his bikes? No, they ___.
Is this your wallet? Yes, it _____.
Are you a witness? No, I'm _____.
Is he a suspect? Yes, he _____.
'These' is used for one object far away.
Short answers repeat the full sentence.
Empareja el demostrativo con su uso

reading.title: A Stolen Bicycle
reading.text: Yesterday, Carlos's bicycle was stolen outside his house. He called the police right away. A police officer arrived quickly and asked questions. 'Is this your bicycle?' he asked, showing a photo. 'Yes, it is!' said Carlos. A neighbor was a witness — she saw a young man take the bicycle. 'Is he a suspect?' asked the officer. 'Yes, he is,' said the neighbor. 'I can describe him.' The officer wrote a report. Carlos was worried, but the officer said the neighborhood is usually very safe. Two days later, the police found the bicycle near the police station.

questions.q: What happened to Carlos's bicycle?
Who saw the thief take the bicycle?
Is the neighborhood usually dangerous?
Where did the police find the bicycle?
Did the officer write a report?

reading.title: At the Police Station
reading.text: Ana lost her wallet yesterday. She went to the police station to report it. 'Is this your ID?' the officer asked, showing a wallet someone found. 'Yes, it is! Thank you so much!' said Ana. The officer explained that a taxi driver found the wallet and brought it to the station. Ana was very happy. She said the city is very safe because people help each other. The officer smiled and said, 'These are the good stories we like to hear.' Ana thanked the officer again and went home.

questions.q: What did Ana lose?

Was Ana happy?
What does Ana say about the city?

listening.title: A Witness Interview
listening.transcript:
A: Are you a witness to the crime?
B: Yes, I am. I saw everything.
A: Can you describe the suspect?
B: Yes. He is tall, and he has a black bag.
A: Is this the bag? (showing a photo)
B: Yes, it is! That's exactly it.
A: Thank you. This information is very helpful.
B: I hope you find him soon.

Empareja quién dice qué

title: Art
grammar_topic: Verb to be: afirmativo, Yes/No questions y contractions
can_do: Puede describir personas/situaciones sencillas y hablar de entretenimiento

grammar_explanation.core_rule: Las contracciones combinan el pronombre y el verbo 'to be' en una sola palabra (I am → I'm). Las preguntas Yes/No con 'to be' invierten el orden: el verbo va antes del sujeto.

structure_notes.label: Contracciones afirmativas
structure_notes.explanation: I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're.
structure_notes.example: She's a painter.

structure_notes.label: Contracciones negativas
structure_notes.explanation: isn't, aren't ('am not' no se contrae, se dice 'I'm not').
structure_notes.example: They're not musicians. / They aren't musicians.

structure_notes.label: Preguntas Yes/No
structure_notes.explanation: Verbo + sujeto + resto de la oración.
structure_notes.example: Is she an artist? Are they musicians?

examples: She's a painter.
They're not musicians.
Is this song popular?
Are you an art student?
grammar_explanation.common_mistake: Intentar contraer 'am not' como 'amn't' — esa forma no existe, se dice 'I'm not'.

grammar_practice.q: He ___ not a singer. (contracción negativa de 'is not')
We ___ not at the concert. (contracción negativa de 'are not')
He _____ a singer, he's an actor.
'Amn't' is a correct contraction of 'am not'.
Empareja la forma completa con su contracción

vocabulary.example: This painting is very famous.
She is a talented artist.
We visited the art museum.
This is my favorite song.
The concert was amazing.
They are in a rock band.
He is a famous actor.
This movie is very popular.
The exhibition is at the museum.
She is a famous singer.
He is very talented.
They perform every weekend.

vocab_practice.q: Where do you go to see paintings?
They are in a rock ___. (grupo musical)
Empareja la palabra con su significado
An 'exhibition' is a type of song.
This ___ is very famous. (obra de arte)
A 'concert' is a live music event.
Which word describes someone with a lot of skill?
Empareja la persona con su actividad

reading.title: A Visit to the Museum
reading.text: Yesterday, my class visited the city's art museum. There is a new exhibition of paintings from local artists. Our teacher says the artist is very talented and famous nationally. One painting is very big and colorful. Is it popular? Yes, it is! Many people take photos next to it. My friend Sara is an art student, and she loves this museum. She says she wants to be an artist too. The museum isn't far from our school, so we walk there every year. It's one of my favorite places to visit.

questions.q: What did the class visit?
Is the artist famous?
Who wants to be an artist?
Is the museum far from the school?
___ this painting popular? (completa)

reading.title: My Favorite Band
reading.text: My favorite band is called Luna Nueva. They're from Sydney, and they're very talented. Their songs are popular all over the country. I'm a big fan, and I have all their music. Last month, they performed at a big concert in my city. It wasn't cheap, but it was worth it! The singer is famous, but she's very humble too. My sister isn't a fan of their music, but she came with me anyway. It was an amazing night, and I hope they perform here again soon.

questions.q: Where is the band from?
Are the band's songs popular?
Is the singer humble?
Is the writer's sister a fan of the band?
They're ___ Sydney. (completa la preposición)

listening.title: At the Art Exhibition
listening.transcript:

title: Buying and Selling
grammar_topic: Be en pasado: afirmativo, negativo y preguntas; count/non-count nouns
can_do: Puede hablar de compras y situaciones pasadas, describir productos, aceptar/rechazar invitaciones

grammar_explanation.core_rule: El pasado del verbo 'to be' es was/were — funciona igual que am/is/are pero para el pasado. Tambien repasamos sustantivos contables (tienen plural: shirt/shirts) y no contables (no tienen plural: money, no 'moneys') porque en compras se usan constantemente juntos.

structure_notes.label: was/were afirmativo
structure_notes.explanation: I/he/she/it + was; you/we/they + were.
structure_notes.example: The store was closed yesterday.

structure_notes.label: was/were negativo
structure_notes.explanation: wasn't / weren't.
structure_notes.example: The shoes weren't expensive.

structure_notes.label: was/were preguntas
structure_notes.explanation: Was/Were + sujeto + ...?
structure_notes.example: Was the sale good this year?

structure_notes.label: sustantivos contables
structure_notes.explanation: Tienen plural, se cuentan con numeros: a/an, two, three...
structure_notes.example: I bought two shirts and a jacket.

structure_notes.label: sustantivos no contables
structure_notes.explanation: No tienen plural. Se usan con some/any/much/a lot of.
structure_notes.example: I don't have much money left.

examples: The market was full of people on Saturday.
There weren't any discounts last week.
Were the prices high at that store?
I bought some fruit and three apples.
exceptions: 'You' siempre usa 'were', incluso hablando de una sola persona: 'You were late', nunca 'you was' — error comun por analogia informal.
grammar_explanation.common_mistake: Usar 'was' con sujetos plurales (they was, we was) o confundir 'money' como contable (a money, moneys) — es no contable.

grammar_practice.q: They ___ not happy with the price.

vocabulary.example: This store has great prices.

reading.text: Last Saturday, I went to the market with my mother. It was very crowded because there was a big sale. We wanted to buy some fruit and vegetables, but the lines were long. There weren't many discounts on fruit, but the vegetables were cheap. My mother bought some tomatoes, two kilos of potatoes, and a bag of onions. I bought a new shirt from a small shop near the entrance. It was brand new and not very expensive. The seller was very friendly and gave us a small discount because we bought a lot. Later, we were tired, so we sat down and had some coffee. It was a good day, even though it was very busy. Next time, I want to go earlier so the lines aren't so long.

title: Education
grammar_topic: Present Perfect; contraste del Present Perfect con otros tiempos
can_do: Puede hablar de experiencias y acciones pasadas relevantes para el presente y hablar de educacion/trabajo

grammar_explanation.core_rule: El Present Perfect (have/has + participio pasado) conecta el pasado con el presente: se usa para experiencias de vida o acciones pasadas cuyo resultado importa AHORA, sin decir exactamente cuando pasaron. Si dices CUANDO exactamente (yesterday, last year, in 2020), tienes que usar Past Simple, no Present Perfect.

structure_notes.label: afirmativo
structure_notes.explanation: have/has + participio.
structure_notes.example: She has finished her degree.

structure_notes.label: negativo
structure_notes.explanation: haven't/hasn't + participio.
structure_notes.example: I haven't applied for that job yet.

structure_notes.label: preguntas
structure_notes.explanation: Have/Has + sujeto + participio...?
structure_notes.example: Have you ever worked abroad?

structure_notes.label: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
structure_notes.explanation: Present Perfect = sin tiempo especifico / relevante ahora. Past Simple = tiempo especifico mencionado.
structure_notes.example: I have graduated (en algun momento) vs. I graduated in 2020 (tiempo especifico).

examples: I have worked in marketing for three years.
She hasn't started her new job yet.
Have you ever studied abroad?
He graduated last year. (NO 'he has graduated last year')
exceptions: 'Ever' y 'never' se usan para hablar de experiencia general en la vida, casi siempre con Present Perfect: 'Have you ever worked in a restaurant?' — nunca con Past Simple con este sentido.
'Just', 'already' y 'yet' acompañan frecuentemente al Present Perfect: 'I have just finished my degree' (recien), 'I haven't finished yet' (todavia no).
grammar_explanation.common_mistake: Usar Present Perfect con una fecha o tiempo especifico: 'I have graduated in 2020' es incorrecto — debe ser 'I graduated in 2020' (Past Simple).

grammar_practice.q: I ___ not started my new job yet.

vocabulary.example: She graduated from university last year.

reading.title: From Classroom to Career
reading.text:
Laura has always been interested in technology. She studied computer science at university and graduated three years ago. Since then, she has worked for two different companies, and she has learned a lot about the software industry.

Her first job was an internship at a small startup. She hasn't forgotten how nervous she felt on her first day. 'I had never worked in a real company before,' she says. 'I had a lot to learn.' During that internship, she gained practical experience that her university courses hadn't fully prepared her for.

After six months, she applied for a full-time position at a larger company. She has been there for over two years now, and she has already received one promotion. 'I've learned that qualifications on paper aren't everything,' she explains. 'Employers also want to see that you can apply what you know.'

Laura's advice for students who haven't started their careers yet is simple: get as much practical experience as possible, even before graduating. 'I did an internship every summer during university,' she says. 'That experience has helped me more than any single class.' She also recommends applying for scholarships and taking on projects outside of regular coursework whenever possible.

title: Couples
grammar_topic: Past modals: should have, could have, might have, may have, must have
can_do: Puede especular sobre situaciones pasadas, expresar arrepentimiento/critica y formular opiniones sobre acontecimientos pasados

grammar_explanation.core_rule: Los modales en pasado (modal + have + participio pasado) sirven para hablar de cosas que NO pasaron pero pudieron pasar, para criticar o lamentar decisiones pasadas, o para especular sobre algo que probablemente pasó. No confundir con 'have to' en pasado ('had to'), que es obligacion real, no especulacion.

structure_notes.label: should have + participio
structure_notes.explanation: Critica o arrepentimiento sobre algo que NO se hizo pero debio hacerse.
structure_notes.example: You should have told me about the wedding. (No me dijiste, y fue un error.)

structure_notes.label: shouldn't have + participio
structure_notes.explanation: Critica sobre algo que SI se hizo pero fue un error hacerlo.
structure_notes.example: She shouldn't have canceled the engagement over text. (Lo hizo, y estuvo mal.)

structure_notes.label: could have + participio
structure_notes.explanation: Una posibilidad o habilidad que existio pero no se uso.
structure_notes.example: He could have proposed sooner, but he waited two years.

structure_notes.label: might have / may have + participio
structure_notes.explanation: Especulacion incierta sobre el pasado — no estamos seguros.
structure_notes.example: They might have broken up because of the distance. We're not sure.

structure_notes.label: must have + participio
structure_notes.explanation: Deduccion casi segura basada en evidencia.
structure_notes.example: She must have forgiven him — they're back together now.

examples: You should have called before showing up. (critica)
I could have married her, but I wasn't ready. (oportunidad no tomada)
He might have cheated, but nobody really knows. (especulacion incierta)
They must have had a huge argument — they haven't spoken in months. (deduccion casi segura)
exceptions: 'must have' NO se niega con 'mustn't have' para deduccion. Para negar una deduccion casi segura se usa 'can't have' o 'couldn't have': 'He can't have forgotten our anniversary' (NO 'He mustn't have forgotten...').

'could have' tambien puede expresar una queja sarcastica ('You could have asked!' = ¡Pudiste haber preguntado!), distinto de su uso como posibilidad neutral — el tono cambia el significado, no la gramatica.
grammar_explanation.register_notes: En ingles hablado, estas formas casi siempre se contraen y se pronuncian 'should've' (sueldan como 'shoulda'), 'could've', 'might've'. En escritura formal o academica SIEMPRE se escriben completas: 'should have', nunca 'should of' (error ortografico comun incluso entre hablantes nativos, por la pronunciacion identica a 'should've').
grammar_explanation.common_mistake: Usar el verbo base en vez del participio: 'She must have go' en vez de 'She must have gone'. Tambien escribir 'should of' en vez de 'should have', copiando la pronunciacion.

grammar_practice.q: You look upset. What happened? — I _____ my phone somewhere. I can't find it.
She ___ have told him earlier — now it's too late. (critica)
He wasn't at the party. He _____ had to work late.
I ___ have helped you if you had asked. (oportunidad no aprovechada)
That's not Marta's coat. It _____ have been left by a guest.

reading.title: Why We Almost Didn't Get Married
reading.text:
Two weeks before our wedding, I called my fiance and told him I wasn't sure anymore. In hindsight, I could have handled it better — a phone call at eleven at night probably wasn't the ideal moment. But I had been having second thoughts for months, and I couldn't keep pretending everything was fine.

My friends had mixed reactions. Some said I should have spoken up much sooner, before we'd already booked the venue and sent the invitations. Others thought I was simply panicking, and that plenty of people must have felt exactly the same way before their own weddings. Maybe they're right. Getting married is a huge decision, and it would be strange NOT to feel nervous.

What surprised me most was my fiance's reaction. He didn't get angry. He said that if I'd stayed quiet just to avoid an awkward conversation, we might have ended up divorced within a few years anyway — and that would have hurt far more than one difficult phone call. He might have been more upset than he showed, but he never let it seem that way.

We postponed the wedding by six months, not canceled it. During that time, we talked more honestly than we ever had before — about money, about where we wanted to live, about whether we both actually wanted children. Looking back, I think we shouldn't have rushed into wedding planning in the first place without having those conversations. We must have assumed that love alone would sort out the rest.

We got married eventually, in a small ceremony with close family only. It wasn't the wedding either of us had originally planned, but I don't regret the delay. If I hadn't made that phone call, we could have gone through with a wedding neither of us was fully ready for. Sometimes the right decision doesn't look like progress at the time.

questions.q: Why does the writer say she 'could have handled it better'?
options: Because she called too late at night
Because she never told her fiance
Because she canceled the wedding completely
Because she told her friends first
questions.answer: Because she called too late at night

questions.q: What did some of her friends think she should have done?
options: Spoken up before booking the venue
questions.answer: Spoken up before booking the venue

questions.q: How did the fiance react to the phone call?
options: He got angry and ended the engagement
He stayed calm and wanted to talk honestly
He refused to speak to her again
questions.answer: He stayed calm and wanted to talk honestly

questions.q: What can we infer about why the couple 'must have assumed love alone would sort out the rest'?
options: They had discussed everything in detail beforehand
They hadn't had important practical conversations before planning the wedding
They didn't want to get married at all
questions.answer: They hadn't had important practical conversations before planning the wedding

questions.q: Did the couple cancel the wedding completely?
According to the text, what does the writer believe now, looking back?
options: She wishes she had never called her fiance
The delay was the right decision, even though it didn't feel that way at the time
She wishes they had married on the original date
questions.answer: The delay was the right decision, even though it didn't feel that way at the time

listening.title: What Happened to Marco and Elena?
listening.transcript:
A: Did you hear about Marco and Elena? They broke up.
B: What? I thought they were about to get married! What happened?
A: I don't really know the details, but apparently they'd been arguing a lot.
B: That's strange, they always seemed so happy together. She must have been really hurt.
A: Yeah, I heard she found out he'd been talking to his ex-partner again.
B: Talking, or... cheating? Because those are very different things.
A: I'm not sure, honestly. He might have just been catching up with her, or it could have been more than that. Nobody really knows for sure.
B: Well, he shouldn't have kept it a secret either way. That's probably what hurt her the most — not knowing.
A: True. If he'd just told her from the start, she might have understood. Instead, she found out from someone else.
B: That would explain why she's so upset. Trust is hard to rebuild once it's broken like that.
A: Exactly. I heard they tried to make up, but it didn't work out.
B: That's really sad. They seemed like soulmates to everyone else, at least.
A: Sometimes things aren't what they look like from the outside.

questions.q: What happened between Marco and Elena?
Why does speaker B say Elena 'must have been really hurt'?
options: Because it's a reasonable deduction based on the situation
questions.answer: Because it's a reasonable deduction based on the situation

What does speaker B think Marco should NOT have done?
options: Talked to his ex-partner at all
Kept the contact a secret from Elena
questions.answer: Kept the contact a secret from Elena

options: She found out from someone else

questions.answer: She found out from someone else

questions.answer: They seemed happy and like soulmates to others

writing.prompt: Escribe una entrada de blog (120-180 palabras) reflexionando sobre una decision del pasado — real o inventada — relacionada con una relacion (pareja, amistad o familia). writing.example_answer: Looking back, I think I could have handled my first serious breakup very differently. At the time, I was convinced I had done nothing wrong, but in hindsight, I probably should have listened more instead of trying to defend myself in every conversation. We must have had the same argument a dozen times without ever really solving anything. I sometimes wonder if we might have stayed together if we'd talked to someone — a friend, a counselor, anyone outside the relationship. We never did, and eventually we just grew apart. I shouldn't have assumed that love was enough to fix everything on its own. These days, I try to remember that a relationship takes more than good intentions.

rubric.descripcion: Reflexiona claramente sobre una decision pasada relacionada con una relacion, con una idea central identificable.

Usa al menos 3 palabras/expresiones de la lista de vocabulario de forma natural.
Las ideas fluyen logicamente, con conectores apropiados entre oraciones.
Mantiene un tono coherente con una entrada de blog personal (semi-informal, reflexivo).

quiz.q: Which sentence uses the CORRECT informal spoken contraction?
